pointOfInterests.description: This is the start of Cataract Canyon. Life jackets are required from here through the last active rapid on Powell Reservoir.
pointOfInterests.name: Confluence- Green/Colorado Rivers

pointOfInterests.description: Hole in the center at low water with an easy line around the right. The beach below this rapid on river right is a nice camp and has a trail upstream of camp that provides access to the Dollhouse.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 1 - Brown Bettie

pointOfInterests.description: Rocks to the left at low water; go center right.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 2

pointOfInterests.description: Straightforward rapid with a line center-right.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 3

pointOfInterests.description: Long rapid with rocks at the right at low water.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 4

pointOfInterests.description: Some big rocks are exposed on the right at low water and a good line is down the left.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 6

pointOfInterests.description: A longer but straightforward rapid that comes right after Rapid 6. The river bends around to the left and then back to the right. Just follow the main current.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 7

pointOfInterests.description: This rapid offers a couple options and has a few rocks to avoid at low water and a wall at the bottom right. Down the right side is good.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 8

pointOfInterests.description: Easy rapid down the middle.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 9

pointOfInterests.description: Rapid 10 comes in quick succession after the previous rapid and features a big wave at low water that is fun surfing for the kayakers and a good hit for rafts. There are some good camps in this area. The Upper X/Y Canyon R Camp is between Rapid 9 and 10, Middle X/Y Canyon R is at the top of Rapid 10, and Lower X/Y Canyon R is adjacent to this surf wave in Rapid 10. A relatively calm stretch of river follows Rapid 10 before the actions starts to pick up again about 3 miles downstream.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 10

pointOfInterests.description: Rapid 11 is a relatively inconsiquential riffle.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 11

pointOfInterests.description: This is a relatively easy rapid where the channel is constrained by debris from the side canyon river left.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 12

pointOfInterests.description: This rapid is formed by outwash from Range Canyon that comes in from river right. It's a relatively straightforward rapid that begins the fun sequence of approximately 3 miles of whitewater that ends with the Big Drop Rapids.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 13

pointOfInterests.description: Beware of the hole in the center. This rapid is also formed by outwash from Range Canyon.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 14

pointOfInterests.description: Several midstream boulders and a line down center right.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 15

pointOfInterests.description: Midstream boulder at low water.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 16

pointOfInterests.description: Easy rapid down the middle.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 17

pointOfInterests.description: Fun waves and hydraulics.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 18

pointOfInterests.description: The river splits around an island. Take the river right channel; the run is left of center with holes and pour overs on the left and right.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 20 - Ben Hurt

pointOfInterests.description: Big Drop 1 represents the start of the most signficiant stretch of whitewater in Cataract Canyon. At lower flows you can read and run down this rapid but at higher flows most pull out above this rapid on the left and scout the whole sequence of whitewater through Big Drop 3.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 21 - Big Drop 1

pointOfInterests.description: Big Drop 2 requires either hard left to right below the marker hole/rock or right to left pull between the marker hole/rock and Little Niagra. Either one reqires a run of the ledge wave. Hit this square. The left to right move is prefered at lower levels (below 40,000 cfs). At high water there are sneak runs but they are not without consequences. The low water scout is on river left above the rapid. At high water it is usually scouted from the left above Big Drop 1 and running all 3 Big Drops at once.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 22 - Big Drop 2

pointOfInterests.description: The biggest rapid on the river. At high water the run is down the right as Satan's Gut forms on the right. At low water a good raft line opens up on the left but there are consequences on either side of the line so it's a good idea to scout. Kayaks have a few more options with lines on the left or right.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 23 - Big Drop 3, Satan's Gut

pointOfInterests.description: Fun read and run down the middle.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 24

pointOfInterests.description: Fun read and run down the middle.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 25

pointOfInterests.description: This rapid has a midstream island. Take the right channel and enjoy fun waves. It takes its name from Don Harris who found two nickels in the sand.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 26 - Ten Cent Rapid

pointOfInterests.description: Long rapid at the mouth of Imperial Canyon with big waves at the bottom. The rapid came and went as reservoir levels fluctuated throughout the 1980's and 1990's. It is the first place where significant reservoir deposits are observed, known as the Dominy Formation, and the transition to the Returned Rapids area.
pointOfInterests.name: Rapid 27 - Imperial Rapid

pointOfInterests.description: A short distinct break after the rapid above marks Short Rapid. Enjoy the fun waves down the middle in the narrowest part of Cataract Canyon.
pointOfInterests.name: Short Rapid

pointOfInterests.description: Easy read and run. This rapid was carved out of the sediment between 2007-2012.
pointOfInterests.name: The Chute

pointOfInterests.description: A wave hole center right.
pointOfInterests.name: Water Hole Canyon Rapid

pointOfInterests.description: A prominent tower on river left that resembles a can opener gives this rapid its name.
pointOfInterests.name: Can Opener Rapid

pointOfInterests.description: This riffle is close to the first benchmark that the USGS established to measure the rate of change in the area as part of the Returning Rapids Project.
pointOfInterests.name: Benchmark Riffle

pointOfInterests.description: Straightforward riffle.
pointOfInterests.name: La Rue's Riffle

pointOfInterests.description: This rapid first began to appear as a riffle in 2018. As of fall 2021 this rapid marked the carving zone of the Dominy Formation sediments and the last rapid in Cataract Canyon. In 2024 this rapid has become much more signifigant, and should be scouted on the left.

pointOfInterests.description: Not yet showing. Dark Canyon is a major canyon on the left. When the reservoir is low, the river elevation here is about 3540 feet. Before the reservoir was filled, boaters encountered a major rapid here but as of 2021 a riffle was not even visible. The rapid is currently buried beneath the sediment of the Dominy Formation, formed when the sediment-laden water of the Colorado River hit the slackwater of the reservoir. As the reservoir drops, the historic channel may be revealed although the course the river chooses near the Dirty Devil confluence will have implications for the rate that can be expected to occur.

pointOfInterests.description: This take out is on the north side of the reservoir, just downstream of the mouth of the Dirty Devil River on river right. It can be difficult to find a good place to beach because of large areas of mud flats, quicksand, and steep banks. It is also easy to get cars stuck in the soft sand and there have been close calls with vehicles nearly ending up in the river. It is not possible to back a trailer down to river level when the reservoir is low. Outfitters use a winch and series of rollers to pull boats up the steep "ramp." This is generally the only take-out available as Hite Marina is usually inaccessible. Contact the National Park Service about current ramp conditions as they can change quickly.
pointOfInterests.name: North Wash Boat Ramp - Dirty Devil Confluence

pointOfInterests.description: Except on very high water years that fill the reservoir this ramp on river left downstream of the Dirty Devil confluence is not accessible. The concrete ramp is generally high and dry, with several hundred feet of mud flat between it and the channel.
pointOfInterests.name: Hite Marina boat ramp

photos.description:
4wd road (BY45): 5 miles Hiking route: 3 miles

This cross-country route is not easy to follow, and going off-track usually leads to a large cliff. Remnants of an old mining road that appears to be built by hand gives hints as to the right direction at times, but I strongly discourage people from trying to just "figure it out" on this route.
That said, it is likely the best option for kayakers and packrafters looking to hike in straight to just above the start of Cataract and cut out the days of flatwater upstream. There was nothing technical about the hike, other than one short wash drop that we passed boats down, and of course the challenging route finding.

detail.permitInfo: Permits are required year-round for all overnight river trips and available by reservation with mid April to mid October launch dates made available the December prior and mid October to mid April launch dates made available the June prior.
detail.description:
The Colorado River cuts an impressive course through Cataract Canyon creating an exciting big water experience. Although faster runs can be made, four to five day trips departing from Potash Boat Ramp downstream of Moab make for a 100 river mile trip that provides a balance between quiet floating, impressive geology, prehistory in canyon country, cool hikes, beach camping, and fast-paced rapids. The trip is an all-around river adventure with spectacular scenery. While this is a great trip for intermediate boaters during the summer or fall, the flows of spring snowmelt provide a high water challenge that should only be attempted by expert big water boaters. The Colorado River through Cataract Canyon at 50,000 cfs is extremely big, pushy, and powerful. The rapids come in quick succession with no recovery time making long swims in cold water a very real possibility.

Cataract Canyon begins just below the confluence of the Green and Colorado Rivers in Canyonlands National Park but this location is not accessible by vehicle. Paddlers have a few options that include boating approximately 50 miles down Meander Canyon of the Colorado (from the Potash Boat Ramp near Moab) or Stillwater Canyon of the Green (from Mineral Bottom Access). Kayakers may be able to arrange a jet boat shuttle from Potash Boat Ramp to Spanish Bottom to avoid the flatwater paddle in. Another option, popular with packrafters, is to hike in from the east along one of the trails in the National Park that provides access to Spanish Bottom.

Beginning at the confluence of the Green and Colorado Rivers, the river is flat for the first three miles before the rapids start and remain more or less constant until the reservoir drowns the river. A short flatwater section (1.5 miles) between rapid 12 and rapid 13 is the prelude to the Mile Long Rapids; this section culminates in the Big Drop Rapids. Scouting Big Drops 2 and 3 at all water levels is recommended. At low water these drops can be scouted individually. At high water paddlers should consider the long scout of the whole sequence from above Big Drop 1 through the bottom of Big Drop 3. After the Big Drops you leave Canyonlands National Park and enter the reservoir-impacted reach of the National Recreation Area. With the continuing drought and decreased reservoir levels, several more good rapids can be enjoyed and you can find the latest information through the [Returning Rapids Project](https://www.returningrapids.com/). Be aware, if it has been a while since you have been down there the returning rapids are quickly changing and will require your attention.

The one big negative of the trip is the end. The waters of Powell have inundated several of the lower rapids below the National Park Boundary. With low reservoir levels you will find current all the way to the Dirty Devil but the approxmiately 30 miles of flatwater after Gypsum Creek Rapid can be challenging especically with the frequent up-canyon winds. Most groups bring a small motor to provide assistance on the trip out. You can row out but pulling into head wind on water with no current can ruin an otherwise excellent trip.
